Art in all or nearly all its forms here finds trusty exponents. The matter is contemporaneous as well as mediseval and ancient. Regarding present-day subjects, it is noticeable that a considerable amount of space is devoted to exhibitions _atJlome andj abroad, the result being that a fair knowledge may be gained of what our neighbours are. _doing, as well as ourselves_. The Royal Academy report, and that on the Paris Salon are of remarkable interest, but the treasures gathered together at the Glasgow Exhibition claimed more than ordinary attention this year, and so, justly, they have been carefully described. The reviews of artbooks given in the Journal are generally good, and are cosmopolitan as well. This is as it should be, for we are too prone to be insular in our ideas. Without exaggeration we may say that the volume of the Art Journal for 1888 is unparalleled as a work of reference in Art, In the foregoing notice we have mentioned the subject of exhibitions.
